lead.label: 2j
lead.why: Abstract: 'Analogues 2j and 2k had the best antipromastigote activities with submicromolar IC50 values'. The abstract names two; 2j is chosen because it has the lowest IC50 in the paper (0.19 uM vs L. major) while 2k is best only against L. donovani (0.73 vs 0.78 uM for 2j). 2k (4-chloro analogue) has the identical two-step route with 2-(4-chlorophenoxy)ethanol.

reactions.conditions: Glycol (11 mmol, 3 equiv) in anhydrous CHCl3 (30 mL), 0 C; PBr3 (3.69 mmol, 1 equiv) dropwise; warm to rt then reflux 60 C 12 h; water quench, DCM extraction, NaHCO3 wash, dried; crude oil used without purification (yield 70-90% for the series).
reactions.source: main text 4.1.2 'Synthesis of brominated ethylene glycol intermediates (1a-o)' and 2.1 Chemistry

reactions.conditions: NFT (2 mmol) in anhydrous DMF (10 mL), Et3N (3 equiv), rt 1 h; then bromide 1j (2 equiv), rt 48 h; solvent removed, column (DCM/MeOH 10:1); yield 10%.
reactions.source: main text 4.1.3 'Synthesis of ethylene glycol nitrofurantoin derivatives (2a-o)'; data for 2j

notes: The paper never prints the name of the glycol or of bromide 1j; both are inferred from the printed name of 2j (3-[2-(4-bromophenoxy)ethyl]), which leaves no doubt about the 2-(4-bromophenoxy)ethyl group. General Methods say 'all chemicals and reagents were purchased', so 2-(4-bromophenoxy)ethanol and nitrofurantoin are taken as commercial. The route is described as general procedures for 1a-o and 2a-o; 1j is used as a crude oil. Step 1 is called 'Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky' in the paper but is an alcohol-to-bromide conversion with PBr3. Two bromide atoms in 1j: one from PBr3 (the aliphatic one), one retained from the aryl group. Lead choice 2j vs 2k is a near tie.
